Cost Insights:


-


Professional flowerbed installation costs between **$1,000 and $3,000** for your project, based on bed size and design.


-


Your flowerbed type drives maintenance, raised beds help you reach plants, pollinator and xeriscape beds need specific choices.


-


Build your budget around edging, mulch, weed barriers, irrigation, lighting, and accents, since add-ons raise your total.


-


[Hiring a local landscaping professional](https://www.angi.com/nearme/landscaping/) ensures solid soil prep and climate-ready plants, so your flowerbed grows healthy and tidy.


*This article was created using automation technology and thoroughly fact-checked and edited by an Angi Editor in accordance with our*[AI policy](https://www.angi.com/standards/editorial-ai-policy.htm) .


In 2026, the national average cost for flowerbed installation is **$2,000** . Most homeowners pay between **$1,000** and **$3,000** , depending on materials, labor, and design. The final cost reflects the size of your flowerbed, plant selection, and any custom features you choose.


## **Flowerbed Size: How Does Size Affect the Cost?**


Flowerbed size is one of the strongest drivers of installation cost, with most residential projects falling into small (under 50 square feet), medium (50 to 150 square feet), or large (over 150 square feet) categories. Larger beds demand more plants, soil, edging, and labor, pushing your total higher. While bigger projects can sometimes benefit from bulk material pricing, the added labor and complexity typically outweigh those savings. Costs vary by bed size, as the breakdown below shows.


Flowerbed Size (Sq. Ft.) Average Cost in 2026 Cost Range in 2026


50 $750 $500–$1,000


100 $1,500 $1,000–$2,000


150 $2,250 $1,500–$3,000


## **Flowerbed Type: Which Option Fits Your Budget?**


The type of flowerbed you choose shapes both your upfront cost and your long-term maintenance commitment, with options ranging from simple in-ground beds to raised, container, and specialty designs. Costs vary meaningfully by type, so the table below breaks down what each option typically runs.


-


**In-ground beds:** Use existing soil and are cost-effective, but may require extra soil amendment.


-


**Raised beds** : Offer improved drainage and accessibility but cost more due to lumber or stone.


-


**Container beds** : Versatile and mobile but limited in size and can be pricier per square foot.


-


**Specialty beds:** Pollinator, shade, or xeriscape beds often require specific plants or features, raising both material and design costs.


Customization, such as curved shapes, multi-level beds, or built-in irrigation, will also increase the price.


Flowerbed Type Description Average Cost in 2026 Pros Cons


In-ground Directly in soil, minimal structure $1,000–$3,000 Affordable, natural look Soil prep may be extensive


Raised bed Built above ground with wood/stone $200–$1,500 Good drainage, easier access Higher material/labor costs


Container bed Planters or pots, portable $100–$500 per container Flexible placement, easy to move Limited size, dries out quickly


Specialty (e.g., pollinator, xeriscape) Custom plants/features $750–$3,750 Supports wildlife, unique design Custom planning and plants are costly


## **Cost by Location**


Where you live and the specific conditions of your site both influence what you pay for flowerbed installation. Labor rates, material prices, and plant availability all shift by region, with urban areas typically carrying higher labor costs than rural ones. Site-specific factors, such as a front yard with easy access versus a backyard on sloped terrain, can raise both labor and material expenses. Local regulations or HOA rules may also require permits or specific materials, adding further to your total.


## **Flowerbed Installation Cost Factors: What Affects the Price?**


Several factors directly impact your final flowerbed installation cost. Here’s a closer look at what impacts your total.


### **Labor**


Labor for flowerbed installation typically runs **$30 to $100 per hour** or **$5 to $15 per square foot** , depending on the experience of the[landscapers](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-landscaping-cost.htm) , gardeners, or design consultants involved. Some companies charge a minimum service fee, particularly for smaller projects. Complex designs, extensive soil work, or irrigation installation will push labor costs higher, and rates also tend to rise during peak seasons.


### **Permits**


Permits for flowerbed installation are typically only required for major excavation, retaining walls, or permanent irrigation systems, with fees ranging from **$50 to $400** depending on your municipality. Always check with your local building department or HOA before starting work to confirm what approvals are needed.


### **Features**


Adding features will increase your flowerbed installation cost:


-


Edging materials (stone, metal, plastic): **$1 to $25 per linear foot**


-


[Mulch](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-mulch-delivery-and-install-cost.htm) : **$30 to $70 per cubic yard**


-


Weed barriers: **$0.50 to $2 per square foot**


-


[Irrigation systems](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-irrigation-systems-work.htm) : **$500 to $1,500 extra per bed**


-


Lighting: **$100 to $500 per bed**


-


Decorative accents (boulders, statues): **varies by choice**


Premium materials or custom shapes also add to the price.


### **Other Cost Factors**


Design complexity, such as curved or multi-level beds, increases both material waste and labor time, while poor accessibility, including beds far from your driveway, steep slopes, or tight spaces, adds to labor and delivery costs. Site prep work, such as removing old landscaping or[soil testing](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-testing-soil-cost.htm) , will also raise your total, and post-construction cleanup or debris removal may carry an additional charge. If you[hire a landscape designer](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-hiring-landscape-designer-cost.htm) , expect design fees of **$50 to $150 per hour** , and some HOAs or cities require inspections that can add **$50 to $200** to your bill.


## **Flowerbed Additional Costs: What to Budget For**


Keep these extra costs in mind when planning your flowerbed installation project to avoid surprises.


### **Warranties**


Some landscapers offer warranties on plants, materials, or workmanship, typically covering one to three years, and these protections may add 5% to 10% of the project price to your total. Warranties often include plant replacement if they fail within the covered period, but always read the fine print for exclusions before signing.


### **Operating Costs**


Ongoing flowerbed costs include watering, fertilizing, seasonal planting, and pest control, with automated irrigation potentially raising your water bill by **$10 to $30** monthly during peak season. Choosing native or drought-tolerant species can reduce both water use and routine care, while annuals and specialty plants typically demand more frequent attention.


### **Maintenance**


Routine flowerbed maintenance covers weeding, mulching, pruning, and replacing annuals, with professional monthly service running **$500 to $1,200 per year** . Doing the work yourself, or limiting professional visits to spring and summer, will reduce that cost. Raised or specialty beds tend to need more frequent attention than standard in-ground designs.


### **Taxes**


Sales tax may apply to both materials and labor depending on your state, and rates and exemptions vary widely. Check your local regulations before finalizing your budget to avoid unexpected charges on your final bill.


### **Insurance**


Always hire insured professionals to protect yourself from liability during flowerbed installation, since coverage addresses accidents or property damage that may occur on the job. Large or complex projects may require the contractor to carry additional coverage, so ask to see proof of insurance before work begins.


## Why You Should Hire a Landscaper

-

-


Landscapers can properly amend your soil for the best growing conditions.


-


Professional landscapers have the tools and equipment to make larger installations more efficient.


-

## **Flowerbed Replacement vs. Repair**


Sometimes, you can repair a flowerbed instead of replacing it. Repairs are best for issues like dead plants, damaged edging, or compacted soil. Full replacement is recommended for severe weed infestations, poor drainage, or an outdated or failing design.


If your repair costs exceed **50%** of the replacement cost, it’s best to replace the bed. For example, repairing a medium bed (replacing plants, fixing edging, adding soil) may cost **$400 to $800** , while a full replacement could be **$1,000 to $2,000** . Factor in the age of the bed and any plant warranties—older or poorly performing beds are better candidates for replacement.


## **Does Flowerbed Installation Add Value to Your Home?**


Professional flowerbed installation offers a strong return on investment (ROI), often between **50% and 80%** . Flowerbeds create curb appeal, making your home more attractive to buyers. Compared to other landscaping projects, flowerbeds are a cost-effective way to boost value and enjoyment.


Additional benefits include improved safety (clear, well-defined walkways), efficiency (low-maintenance or drought-tolerant designs), and enhanced functionality (pollinator or edible beds). Beautiful, accessible beds can be enjoyed by everyone and make outdoor spaces more inviting.


## **Tips to Reduce Cost While Installing a Flowerbed**


Consider these cost-saving strategies to make your flower bed project more budget-friendly:


-


Choose native or drought-tolerant plants to lower material and maintenance costs.


-


Install flowerbeds during the off-season for potential labor discounts.


-


Source materials locally to reduce delivery fees.


-


DIY simple tasks like mulching or edging to cut labor costs.


-


Get multiple quotes from reputable[local landscapers](https://www.angi.com/nearme/landscaping/) to compare pricing.


-


Opt for simpler designs or smaller beds if on a tight budget.


-


Reuse existing soil or compost where possible.


Next Steps: Finalize Your Project With a Pro


-


Decide what size and style flowerbed you want so you can find a pro who specializes in that type of installation.


-


If you have specific plants in mind, ask the landscaper what features and other plants will best complement them.


-


Be prepared to discuss your budget and how much you want to allocate for specific features.
